items.stem: When calling Azure OpenAI in Azure AI Foundry via the API, which name must you reference?

options.rationale: Correct: Azure OpenAI always requires the deployment name, even in the model parameter.
The subscription ID is not used to select the model in the call.
The resource group is not the model identifier in API calls.
The region is not how the API selects the deployed model.

items.explanation: Correct: Azure OpenAI always requires the deployment name, even in the model parameter.

items.stem: Which TWO are recommended security practices for Azure OpenAI? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Microsoft Entra ID (keyless) authentication where possible
options.rationale: Correct: Entra ID managed identity auth avoids storing keys in code.

options.text: Store any required keys in Azure Key Vault, not in code
options.rationale: Correct: keys should be stored securely and never posted publicly.

options.text: Commit the API key into source control for convenience
options.rationale: Keys must never be committed or posted publicly.

options.text: Disable content filtering to speed responses
options.rationale: Content filtering is a safety control that should not be casually disabled.

items.explanation: Correct: Entra ID managed identity auth avoids storing keys in code.

items.stem: A low-volume pilot needs a simple way to set an effective rate limit on a deployment. Which setting applies?

options.rationale: Correct: TPM quota sets the effective rate limit for a deployment.
Sensitivity labels are a Microsoft 365 data-protection feature, not a TPM limit.

options.text: The workspace capacity SKU for Power BI
options.rationale: That is a Power BI concept, unrelated to Azure OpenAI TPM.
Conditional Access governs sign-in, not model TPM limits.

items.explanation: Correct: TPM quota sets the effective rate limit for a deployment.
